maya: Heads-up — repro'ing weird KV cache memory growth when users hit extended conversations (~50k tokens). Observed sustained page-in activity and eviction thrash. Mostly on Dedicated + Private, sporadic on Hosted. Anyone seen this?

sanjay: Saw a customer hit something similar last week. Tail latencies and p99 token costs shot up. Eviction counters climb, free frames don't coalesce. My gut: batching heuristic expands under long contexts and we end up with massive per-request KV allocations + kernel fallback churn. :thinking: 

linda: Can you paste a small repro / logs and which model/quantization? Also whether Dedicated uses the same jemalloc / hugepage config as Hosted.

maya: Model: redwood-13b-q4_0 (quantized), routing: prefer-fast-kernel then fallback to scalar. Repro command we used:
```
./bench_infer --model redwood-13b-q4_0 --tokens 50000 --concurrency 4 --session-accumulate true --enable-kv-cache
```
Partial memstat snapshot (Dedicated):
```
KV_resident_pages: 324512
KV_eviction_count: 18294
Pagefaults/sec: 230
Fragmentation_ratio: 1.82
Kernel_fast_count: 1853
Kernel_scalar_count: 4571
```

sanjay: That Kernel_scalar_count looks telling — on some on-prem GPUs older drivers force scalar paths. Scalar kernels allocate intermediate buffers differently and block reuse. Also check NIC/MTU in VPC — small MTUs + GSO off can increase RPC batching and cause bigger KV batches.

ops-bot: config-drift-detector: noticed mismatch for cluster "dedicated-eu-03": jemalloc.background_thread = false (Hosted=true). Flagged at 2026-03-17T09:12Z.

toni: If batching window grows with conversation length we should cap per-request KV growth. Proposal: add kv_target_resident and per-session kv_growth_limit. Example config: 
```json
{"kv_target_resident": 256000, "kv_growth_limit_tokens": 2048}
```
This would force earlier eviction / compression rather than letting memory spiral.

linda: Did a quick profile on Hosted vs Dedicated (small run). Summary: Hosted: avg resident pages/request ~ 18k, Kernel_fast ratio ~ 0.6. Dedicated (customer image): resident pages/request ~ 42k, Kernel_fast ratio ~ 0.22, pagefault spikes aligned with driver fallback events. Reuse score (how often we hit existing prefix frames) drops after ~20k tokens.

maya: So pattern: long sessions -> batching heuristic increases request window -> allocator hands out many frames -> fragmentation + fallback kernels reduce reuse -> evictions thrash. Config drift (jemalloc off, different hugepage) + VPC/network differences amplify on Dedicated/Private.

sanjay: Actionable repro steps: 1) run bench_infer with --session-accumulate true for 50k tokens on Dedicated image, 2) capture /proc/<pid>/smaps, jemalloc stats: `je-ctl stats`, 3) perf record -e cpu-clock -g -- ./bench... and nvprof / CUPTI for kernel selection timeline. Also capture driver version: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv`.

linda: Quick mitigation suggestions: - enforce smaller batching window for sessions beyond N tokens - enable jemalloc background_thread + decay settings (same as Hosted) - add early KV compaction pass when fragmentation_ratio > 1.5 - force fast-kernel fallback threshold tuned per-GPU capability.

maya: Can we test a canary: Dedicated cluster with jemalloc.background_thread=true + kv_growth_limit_tokens=2048? ops-bot can you schedule a canary?

ops-bot: schedule: canary deploy to dedicated-eu-03 with overrides applied: jemalloc.background_thread=true, kv_growth_limit_tokens=2048. Canary window 1h starting 2026-03-18T14:00Z. Will report metrics to #eng-runtime.

toni: I'll open a PR with config knobs and an eval that simulates extended-conversation accumulation to guard regressions. Also adding a kernel-selection metric to telemetry (fast/scalar ratio per model).

sanjay: I'll take perf traces on the customer's Dedicated image Thursday. If we confirm driver-induced scalar fallbacks, ops should coordinate driver upgrade or pin a fast-kernel-compatible runtime.

linda: One more data point — Private (on-prem) node had VFIO pinned frames and older kernel, we saw persistent non-coalescing pages. Could need a reclaim path that does cross-frame compaction rather than naive eviction.

maya: Great. Summary: repro confirmed patterns, likely multifactor (batching growth + allocator config drift + kernel fallback + VPC/MTU effects). Next: canary, perf traces, PR for kv caps + telemetry. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: noted actions: create ticket INF-8272 (mmap/evict investigation), assign to eng-runtime team, link perf artifacts after runs.
